subject: science
skillName: Speed and the Energy of Motion
intro: A moving object has energy of motion. The faster an object moves, the more energy of motion it has. We can see this energy when a moving object hits something: a fast-moving ball can knock over more pins, push an object farther, or make a bigger dent than the same ball moving slowly. So speed is evidence of energy. When two objects have the same size and shape, the faster one carries more energy, and the slower one carries less.

items.prompt: A bowling ball rolled fast knocks down all the pins, but the same ball rolled slowly knocks down only a few. What does this tell you about speed and energy?

steps: The energy of a moving object shows up in what it can do when it hits something.
The fast ball knocked down more pins than the slow ball, so it did more.
This is evidence that the faster the ball moves, the more energy of motion it has.
solution.answer: The faster the ball moves, the more energy of motion it has, so it knocks down more pins.

items.prompt: Two identical toy cars roll into a block. Car A is moving fast and pushes the block far. Car B is slow and barely moves the block. Explain the difference using energy.

steps: A moving car carries energy of motion that it transfers to the block.
Car A moved the block far, so it transferred more energy; Car B barely moved it, so it had less.
Car A was faster, which is why it had more energy of motion.
solution.answer: Car A is faster, so it has more energy of motion and pushes the block farther.

items.prompt: A student wants evidence that a faster marble has more energy. Describe a test and what result would show this.

steps: Roll the same marble at a target at a slow speed and then at a fast speed.
Measure how far the target moves each time.
If the target moves farther when the marble is faster, that is evidence the faster marble has more energy.
solution.answer: Roll the same marble slow and fast into a target; if the target moves farther with the faster marble, the faster marble has more energy.

items.prompt: Which has more energy of motion: a soccer ball kicked hard and moving fast, or the same ball tapped and moving slowly?

steps: More speed means more energy of motion for the same object.
The hard-kicked ball moves faster than the tapped ball.
So the hard-kicked, fast-moving ball has more energy of motion.
solution.answer: The ball kicked hard and moving fast has more energy of motion.

items.prompt: A faster-flowing river can carry bigger rocks than a slow river. How does this relate speed to energy?

steps: Moving water has energy of motion, and faster water moves faster.
The faster river moves bigger rocks, which takes more energy.
So the faster river has more energy of motion than the slow one.
solution.answer: The faster river has more energy of motion, so it can carry bigger rocks.

items.prompt: A student says a slow and a fast object of the same size have the same energy. Use evidence to correct this.

steps: Energy of motion depends on speed for objects of the same size.
Tests show a faster object knocks things over harder and pushes them farther than a slow one.
So the faster object has more energy, and the claim that they are equal is wrong.
solution.answer: The faster object has more energy because it pushes and knocks things harder, so they are not equal.
